title: Changing protein-DNA interactions promote ORC binding site exchange during replication origin licensing
authors: Annie Zhang; Larry J. Friedman; Jeff Gelles; Stephen P Bell
one_liner_zh: 该文用单分子FRET研究ORC-Mcm2-7复制起始中的蛋白-DNA动态互作与结合位点切换，属广义蛋白-DNA互作机制，但无AI/物理模拟方法，且非TF-DNA体系。
abstract: During origin licensing, the eukaryotic replicative helicase Mcm2-7 forms head-to-head double hexamers to prime origins for bidirectional replication. Recent single-molecule and structural studies revealed that one molecule of the helicase loader ORC can sequentially load two Mcm2-7 hexamers to ensure proper head-to-head helicase alignment. To perform this task, ORC must release from its initial high-affinity DNA binding site and “flip” to bind a weaker, inverted DNA site. However, the mechanism of this binding-site switch remains unclear. In this study, we used single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (sm-FRET) to study the changing interactions between DNA and ORC or Mcm2-7. We found that the loss of DNA bending that occurs during DNA deposition into the Mcm2-7 central channel increases the rate of ORC dissociation from DNA. Further studies revealed temporally-controlled DNA sliding of helicase-loading intermediates, and that the first sliding complex includes ORC, Mcm2-7, and Cdt1. We demonstrate that sequential events of DNA unbending, Cdc6 release, and sliding lead to a stepwise decrease in ORC stability on DNA, facilitating ORC dissociation from its strong binding site during site switching. In addition, the controlled sliding we observed provides insight into how ORC accesses secondary DNA binding sites at different locations relative to the initial binding site. Our study highlights the importance of dynamic protein-DNA interactions in the loading of two oppositely-oriented Mcm2-7 helicases to ensure bidirectional DNA replication. Significance Statement Bidirectional DNA replication, in which two replication forks travel in opposite directions from each origin of replication, is required for complete genome duplication. To prepare for this event, two copies of the Mcm2-7 replicative helicase are loaded at each origin in opposite orientations. Using single-molecule assays, we studied the sequence of changing protein-DNA interactions involved in this process. These stepwise changes gradually reduce the DNA-binding strength of ORC, the primary DNA binding protein involved in this event. This reduced affinity promotes ORC dissociation and rebinding in the opposite orientation on the DNA, facilitating the sequential assembly of two Mcm2-7 molecules in opposite orientations. Our findings identify a coordinated series of events that drive proper DNA replication initiation.
abstract_zh:
在起始许可过程中，真核复制解旋酶Mcm2-7形成头对头的双六聚体，以启动复制起点进行双向复制。近年来的单分子和结构研究揭示，解旋酶装载因子ORC的一个分子可以依次装载两个Mcm2-7六聚体，以确保头对头解旋酶的正确排列。为完成此任务，ORC必须从其初始高亲和力DNA结合位点释放，并“翻转”以结合一个较弱的反向DNA位点。然而，这种结合位点切换的机制仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们使用单分子福斯特共振能量转移（sm-FRET）来研究DNA与ORC或Mcm2-7之间变化的相互作用。我们发现，在DNA沉积到Mcm2-7中央通道过程中发生的DNA弯曲丧失，增加了ORC从DNA解离的速率。进一步研究揭示了解旋酶装载中间体的时间控制性DNA滑动，并且第一个滑动复合物包含ORC、Mcm2-7和Cdt1。我们证明，DNA去弯曲、Cdc6释放和滑动的连续事件导致ORC在DNA上稳定性的逐步降低，从而促进ORC在位点切换过程中从其强结合位点解离。此外，我们观察到的受控滑动为ORC如何访问相对于初始结合位点不同位置的次级DNA结合位点提供了见解。我们的研究强调了动态蛋白质-DNA相互作用在装载两个相反方向的Mcm2-7解旋酶以确保双向DNA复制中的重要性。  
意义声明 双向DNA复制，即每个复制起点处两个复制叉沿相反方向行进，是完整基因组复制所必需的。为准备此事件，每个起点处装载两个相反方向的Mcm2-7复制解旋酶拷贝。利用单分子实验，我们研究了此过程中涉及的蛋白质-DNA相互作用的改变序列。这些逐步变化逐渐降低ORC（此事件中主要DNA结合蛋白）的DNA结合强度。这种降低的亲和力促进ORC解离并以相反方向重新结合到DNA上，从而促进两个Mcm2-7分子以相反方向顺序组装。我们的发现识别了一系列协调事件，驱动正确的DNA复制起始。
